newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila C.Bank will have to help peso - traders.
newsitem.headline: Manila C.Bank will have to help peso - traders.

text.p: There could be a run on on the peso when trading starts on Monday if the Central Bank does not intervene in the market, dealers said.
"It will settle when the Central Bank shows its face," a foreign bank dealer said. "The market is strongly imbalanced. Everything might just go out of hand."
Traders said optimists in the market were looking at 29 pesos per dollar as a good level to sell but it could fall further.
The Bankers Association of the Philippines said on Monday it had suspended its volatility band after the Central Bank on Friday allowed the peso to move within a wider range.
The volatility band allows the temporary halting of trades if the peso moves beyond or below 1-1/2 percent of a reference rate.
The peso fell 11.5 percent on Friday to 29.45 but the bankers group excluded all the deals because the peso had moved beyond the volatility band.
Instead it had insisted Monday's trading would start at 26.40 pesos, the average of Thursday's trading before the effective devaluation and which traders said would cause havoc in the market.
The Central Bank had also urged the volatility band be dropped.
The Central Bank changed its strategy to quell speculation after draining almost $1 billion of its reserves last week and raising its overnight borrowing rate to a 2-1/2 year high.
The peso had come under repeated attack after Thailand's de facto devaluation two weeks ago.
"I suspect the Central Bank will come in at 27.50/28.50," one dealer said.
Trading will start at 9 am (0100 gmt) instead of the usual 8.30 am (0030 gmt)
